newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1997 grain output seen up at 25 mln T -min.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1997 grain output seen up at 25 mln T -min.

text.p: Poland's grain production in 1997 is likely to be slightly higher than in 1996 at 25 million tonnes against 24.7 million last year, the agriculture minister told Reuters on Monday.
"According to preliminary estimates grain production this year will be slightly better than last year and will amount to some 25 million tonnes," Jaroslaw Kalinowski said.
Earlier this month a senior government-linked analyst predicted Poland's 1997 grain output should be 23.4 to 24.5 million tonnes, against demand of 26.2 million.
Analysts said that even if Poland's production was lower than last year the country would easily be able to cover its needs from accumulated reserves reaching four million tonnes.

Kalinowski also said the council of ministers might increase import duty on barley to 20 percent from the current 10 percent at its next meeting on Tuesday while duty on other grains would rise to 20 percent from the current 10 on July 1.
"It is possible that tomorrow the council of ministers will decide to raise duty on barley," Kalinowski said.
Since July 1996, when Poland lowered its 20 percent duty on grain imports to fight grain price rises, imports totalled 3.3 million tonnes.
